answer: Each agent earns transferable credits only by completing a task that a randomly selected peer verifies against a public result; the verifier stakes credits and loses them if later audits overturn its approval. A newcomer can create many identities, but cannot make them productive without doing the work, and colluding verifiers risk their own stake. The credits act as nectar for useful participation, while a bridge connects newcomers to tasks and a reef of independent audits makes cheap identity floods costly to sustain.
